I have all the details. Here is what I found.

## The news list

On the news page, the most recent item listed is dated **2026-09-10** ("Multiplex tissue image of the month – PDX1 in pancreas") — but this is an *Image of the Week* feature, not a report of a study, so it has no journal/team/identification to report.
- Source: https://www.proteinatlas.org/news

The most recent news article that actually reports a study is dated **2026-09-02**.

## What that article reports

The article is titled **"Reducing uncertainty in drug development: a Q&A with Thomas Helleday"** (2026-09-02).

- **Journal the study was published in:** *Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy* (cited as "Manolakou, 2026").
- **Who led the team:** a team led by **Thomas Helleday and Theodora Manolakou**.
- **What they identified:** "a novel, targetable transcriptional-metabolic axis that sustains inflammatory T-cell responses." The Q&A explains this is **MTHFD2-dependent one-carbon metabolism** — inflammatory/activated T cells in rheumatoid arthritis rely on this metabolic machinery, and the compound TH9619 inhibits both MTHFD1 and MTHFD2.

Sources (both statements rest on the 2026-09-02 article page):
- https://www.proteinatlas.org/news/2026-09-02/reducing-uncertainty-in-drug-development-a-q-a-with-thomas-helleday

For completeness, the news page also lists an earlier study-report article (2026-08-27, "The multiplex tissue resource provides deeper spatial insight into protein expression," published in *Protein Science*), but that is not the most recent one.

## Plain answer

The most recent news article on proteinatlas.org that reports a study is the **2026-09-02** piece "Reducing uncertainty in drug development: a Q&A with Thomas Helleday." The study was published in **Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy**; it was **led by Thomas Helleday and Theodora Manolakou**; and they **identified a novel, targetable transcriptional-metabolic axis (MTHFD2-dependent one-carbon metabolism) that sustains inflammatory T-cell responses**.

One caveat: the single most recent item on the news page overall is the 2026-09-10 "Multiplex tissue image of the month – PDX1 in pancreas," but that is an image feature rather than a study report, so it doesn't address the journal/team/identification questions.
